To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) toxic milk mutant mice are animal models of Wilson disease; (2) in toxic milk mutants, a decrease in ferroxidase ceruloplasamin activity leads to a disturbance in iron homeostasis, (3) toxic milk mutants develop functional iron deficiency, and (4) the key role in this phenomenon is played by a decrease in ceruloplasmine expression.
in the toxic milk mutant mice, despite the presence of high levels of ferroporin, a decreased ferroxidase (ceruloplasmin) activity leads to a functional iron deficiency.
in the tx-J mutant mice with disturbed copper metabolism, functional iron deficiency is caused by decreased expression of GPI-ceruloplamin in liver macrophage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploration of the role of ceruloplasticin in iron metabolism and the role of copper metabolism disturbances in iron balance.
the role of ceruloplastic in the regulation of iron homeostasis in the liver.
the mechanisms of iron homeostasis in toxic milk mutant (tx-J) mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Wilson disease and its mouse model (tx-J mice) are not only copper disorders but also iron disorders.
the tx-J mice represent a novel animal model of functional iron deficiency.
the toxic milk mutant mice are a good animal model for exploring the role of ceruloplastic in the control of iron homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tx-J mice are good models for exploring the role of copper in iron metabolism.
the tx-J mouse represents a model of functional iron deficiency in which a decrease in ceruloplasmins expression leads to a decreased release of iron to extracellular fluid.
the tx-J mutants represent a unique model of iron deficiency caused by a defect in copper metabolism.
